issues.legal_issue: A statutory tax exemption may be withdrawn by the government when it acts within its statutory powers to permit the tax to be levied.
material_facts: The municipal committee passed a resolution exempting goods imported into the market from octroi, and the State Government confirmed a later resolution granting that exemption under the statutory procedure.
The State Government subsequently approved the municipal committee’s resolution seeking cancellation of the exemption, after which the municipality began collecting octroi.
The challenge was to the government’s approval and the resulting levy of octroi.
issues.conclusion: The State Government acted within its statutory powers in withdrawing the exemption and permitting the levy, so its action could not be invalidated by estoppel.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 70(2)(c), 62-A and 60(A)(3) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, as amended, empowered the State Government to confirm an exemption, direct the imposition of tax, and act if the municipality failed to comply. A government acting in its statutory functions is not estopped from exercising those powers. The Court relied on Excise Commissioner, U.P. v. Ram Kumar, M. Ramanatha Pillai v. State of Kerala and State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Manufacturing Co. Ltd.

predicates.challenge_to_public_tax_levy: A party challenged a tax levy or governmental action permitting that levy.
predicates.government_acted_within_statutory_power: The government acted within its legal authority in deciding whether the tax exemption should continue.
predicates.government_withdrew_tax_exemption: The government ended an existing exemption from the tax.

issues.definition: When a public tax levy is challenged, a government action withdrawing an exemption within its legal authority is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A public authority is not estopped from acting according to law when its earlier representation exceeded its authority.
material_facts: The municipal committee advertised plots in the market on the representation that octroi would not be imposed there, and purchasers relied on that representation.
The committee’s original promise of continuing immunity from octroi exceeded its authority to exempt property from the tax.
The committee later recommended that the exemption be cancelled and octroi imposed.
issues.conclusion: The municipal committee was not estopped from recommending or imposing octroi because its original promise was beyond its authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 70(2)(c) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, an exemption required a resolution at a special meeting confirmed by the State Government; the municipality could not independently promise permanent immunity from the tax. Estoppel cannot require a public authority to act contrary to law or validate an ultra vires act. The Court relied on Excise Commissioner, U.P. v. Ram Kumar, M. Ramanatha Pillai v. State of Kerala and State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Manufacturing Co. Ltd.

predicates.claim_to_estop_public_authority: A party sought to prevent a public authority from acting by relying on an earlier representation made by that authority.
predicates.public_authority_made_tax_exemption_prom: A public authority represented that a tax would not be imposed on specified persons or property.
predicates.promise_exceeded_authority: The authority lacked legal power to make the tax-exemption promise it gave.

issues.definition: A party cannot use a public authority’s promise to prevent lawful action when the authority lacked power to make that promise.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel may constrain an authorized public officer who arbitrarily repudiates a representation relied on to the promisee’s disadvantage, but it cannot bar legislative or statutory functions or validate unauthorized acts.
material_facts: The purchasers relied on the municipal committee’s representation that octroi would not be imposed in the market and claimed to have purchased plots and built establishments on that basis.
The representation at issue was not an authorized undertaking binding the State Government, and the municipality lacked authority to grant the asserted permanent exemption.
The State Government acted in exercising statutory powers when it approved cancellation of the exemption and permitted the tax levy.
issues.conclusion: Promissory estoppel did not bar the municipal committee or the State Government from acting according to law in this case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that promissory estoppel is unavailable against legislative functions, the discharge of statutory duties, or acts of government officers beyond their authority. Where an authorized officer makes a representation under a scheme and a person relies on it to their disadvantage, a court may require the officer to honour it if the officer repudiates it arbitrarily; the officer may nevertheless change course for special considerations bearing on the State’s general interest. The Court applied Union of India v. Indo-Afghan Agencies Ltd. on authorized representations and arbitrary repudiation, while distinguishing its scope; it relied on Howell v. Falmouth Boat Construction Co. Ltd., Assistant Custodian of Evacuee Property v. Brij Kishore Agarwala, Bihar Eastern Gangetic Fishermen Cooperative Society v. Sipahi Singh, Excise Commissioner, U.P. v. Ram Kumar, M. Ramanatha Pillai v. State of Kerala and State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Manufacturing Co. Ltd. It also considered Article 299(1) of the Constitution, sections 10, 25, 63, 65 and 70 of the Contract Act, and explained and disagreed in part with the approach in Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

rule.if: public_authority_promise_claim and officer_acted_within_authority and promise_made_under_scheme and promisee_relied_to_disadvantage and officer_repudiated_arbitrarily and not_special_public_interest_justification

predicates.public_authority_promise_claim: A party sought to enforce a representation made by a public authority.
predicates.officer_acted_within_authority: The public officer who made the representation acted within the authority given to that officer.
predicates.promise_made_under_scheme: The officer made the representation as part of an applicable public scheme.
predicates.promisee_relied_to_disadvantage: The person to whom the representation was made relied on it and put themselves in a worse position.
predicates.officer_repudiated_arbitrarily: The officer later refused to honour the representation arbitrarily, without a disclosed justification.
predicates.special_public_interest_justification: The authority had a special consideration affecting the general interest of the State that justified changing course.

issues.definition: An authorized scheme-based promise relied on to a person’s disadvantage must be honoured when the authority repudiates it arbitrarily and no special public-interest justification exists.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot claim an enforceable contractual right against a municipality when the required written execution of the contract has not been proved.
material_facts: The purchasers relied on the market-sale proclamation as an undertaking that octroi would not be imposed.
No sale deed executed by the municipal committee in favour of the purchasers was produced, so the contract was not proved to have been reduced to writing and executed in the prescribed manner.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers had no enforceable contractual right under the municipal sale terms.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47 of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, prescribed the manner in which the relevant municipal contract had to be made. Article 299(1) of the Constitution makes its prescribed form and execution requirements mandatory for contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or a State, as a matter of public policy. The Court relied on Seth Bhikraj Jaipuria v. Union of India, Mulamchand v. State of Madhya Pradesh and Karamshi Jethabhai Somayya v. State of Bombay.

predicates.contract_claim_against_municipality: A party claimed a contractual right arising from an arrangement with a municipality.
predicates.prescribed_written_execution_proved: The party proved that the contract was reduced to writing and executed in the manner required for that public-body contract.

issues.definition: A party claiming a contractual right against a municipality has no enforceable right when the required written execution of the contract is not proved.
